speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Thus, I would like to ask the Minister if LTA would consider working with these companies like Ofo and Obike to proliferate the bicycle-sharing scheme and make it popular in all major towns in Singapore, besides just Jurong Lake District, but less the messiness.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I will share how MOT plans to transform it over the longer term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Singaporeans can look forward to a future transport system that will be smarter, greener and more inclusive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will use big data and analytics to improve train reliability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will be deploying condition monitoring tools on our trains and equipment to collect data more extensively and on a real-time basis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will also be deploying a new-generation Automatic Track Inspection System for the Downtown Line.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Imaging sensors and lasers will be installed on revenue trains to scan the tracks of the entire Downtown Line to detect anomalies, so that we can arrest any faults early.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: To enable this transition, we will need to build an integrated asset management database, so that we can better monitor and predict the health of the entire rail network and all its components.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Data analytics are also helping us improve other aspects of our transport system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For instance, the public bus operators track the location of all their buses, and they are applying analytics so that they can instruct their bus captains to either slow down or speed up to avoid bunching with other buses, all in real time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This will, in part, answer Mr Melvin Yong's concerns.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This will enable LTA to better model commuter flows in our public transport network and improve its overall planning capabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We can then also respond more effectively to ground developments, such as by injecting additional bus and rail capacity, to cope with unexpected crowd surges or even train delays.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In time to come, we will be able to integrate private transport data as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Using Global Navigation Satellite System technology and through the in-vehicle units that are installed in all vehicles in Singapore, we can get aggregated, comprehensive and real-time data on road traffic.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We can use it to improve traffic flows, for instance, by providing motorists with access to real-time traffic data to decide on the fastest or least congested routes, and enable even our traffic light system to respond more intelligently and optimally to different real-time road conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Apart from big data, mobile technology is another key enabler in our transport sector and this is already benefiting commuters tremendously.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In particular, just-in-time, demand-responsive transport has become more pervasive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For example, all of us know, just until a few years ago, if we wanted to book a taxi, we had to speak to an operator on the phone, and had access only to the taxis of that one company and this is not including all the holding time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But today, we use an app, like GrabTaxi, to book taxis almost instantaneously from any taxi company.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Commuters are better served because there are now more taxis that are reachable, literally at our fingertips.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But the greater disruptive change by far, enabled by mobile technology, has been private hire car services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: At the same time, it seems that many more commuters are taking point-to-point transportation, both on taxis and in private hire cars.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I am glad to see that commuters are using these mobile technologies and are satisfied with both taxi and private hire car services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Mr Zaqy Mohamad and Miss Cheng Li Hui expressed concerns about dynamic pricing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I am glad that taxi companies and drivers are rising to the competition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Taxi drivers, as I said, have improved their services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Customer satisfaction has improved from a year ago.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: And taxi companies are rethinking their business models.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Some have lowered rental rates and introduced innovative rental schemes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: More recently, I know that they have proposed dynamic pricing as one more option for booked trips.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This is similar to the way fares for private hire car services are determined.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The PTC is currently discussing the details with the taxi companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Meanwhile, my view is that we should let the taxi industry innovate and adapt to the new market conditions and competition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our taxi drivers have to make a living, too, and we should not restrict their ability to compete effectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: On the other hand, I understand some commuters' concerns about dynamic pricing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They can then choose to accept or decline the offer.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For commuters who prefer more familiarity, they will have the traditional option to book a taxi.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The taxi companies, I understand, intend to retain the traditional metered fare system even as they introduce dynamic pricing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But ultimately, taxi companies should ensure that dynamic pricing improves and not worsens the matching of demand and supply.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our light-touch approach has served commuters well so far.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The new regulations for private hire drivers and vehicles are aimed at protecting commuters' interests, especially safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They pay the Category A Prevailing Quota Premium even though many taxis are larger Category B models.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: So, while we try to ensure that competition is fair, it is not always possible and desirable to impose the exact same regulations on both sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There are likely to be further disruptions afield.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The recent trend is ride-sharing among unrelated commuters.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: UberPool and GrabShare offer commuters the possibility of sharing a private hire car trip if they are headed in the same direction, which is cheaper than taking a ride on your own.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We also have SWAT, a local start-up that aims to provide on-demand bus services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The company uses a routing algorithm to pick up and drop off passengers on demand, while dynamically optimising the route real-time so that the bus can manage passengers most efficiently.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This could potentially transform how bus services are operated in the future, including public bus services in areas where there is low ridership and maybe during low-demand hours.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: A few years back, we studied the schemes in cities like London, Paris and New York.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These are the traditional ones with docking stations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We thought they could potentially work in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But, they were however not sustainable commercially and required some Government subsidy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: So, we took some time to work out how to fund this and, eventually, LTA put out a tender last year for a bicycle sharing service, starting small in the Jurong Lake District.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: However, as Mr Ang Wei Neng has observed, in recent months, this has been disrupted almost.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We have seen the emergence of dockless bicycle sharing systems here in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These dockless systems allow users to hire and return a shared bicycle at any location.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There are obvious advantages: lower infrastructure costs, more convenience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It is still not clear whether these new systems or the traditional ones will work better for Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: LTA will study both the docked and dockless systems.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: And we will assess whether to proceed with our plans and whether to extend them to other towns like Ang Mo Kio, as Mr Ang Hin Kee has suggested, given that Ofo and Obike are already rolling out their services independently of LTA's tender.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We are focusing on self-driving technology in a big way because they have the potential to dramatically improve public transport.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For instance, we could have a fleet of self-driving pods or shuttles that can be called on demand to bring us from our doorstep to an MRT station.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Self-driving buses, on the other hand, could address our shortage of bus drivers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Of course, significant technology challenges have still to be overcome before self-driving can take off in a big way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But we are working towards such a day by facilitating the development of such technology and mobility concepts in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We have embarked on trials of self-driving pods.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Initiatives are underway to develop self-driving buses and to explore how the technology can be applied for use in freight transport and utility vehicles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We also launched the Centre of Excellence for Testing & Research of Autonomous Vehicles at NTU (CETRAN) in August last year, to establish a set of safety and performance standards for our local environment as well as testing requirements and protocols.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The advent of these technological innovations and new business models worries our transport workers, quite understandably.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Melvin Yong and Miss Cheng Li Hui all similarly expressed, I understand their concerns as well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But the right approach is to prepare our workers for these changes and not obstruct them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In any case, these technological advances cannot be stopped, and even if slowed, we will lose out on the many new opportunities that they bring along.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will help our workers to upskill and re-skill, so that they can take on the new jobs that will come as the industry evolves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Government has put in place the institutions to do so, with the Singapore Rail Academy and the Singapore Bus Academy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We are working closely with our tripartite partners through platforms, such as the Public Transport Sectoral Tripartite Committee chaired by Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This Committee will identify the relevant skills, build local capabilities and develop the curricula to nurture a future-ready workforce.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For taxi drivers, Mr Ang Hin Kee suggested some incentives to get more taxi drivers to ply the road by waiving their licence renewal fees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will consider Mr Ang's suggestions, but I think what will be more meaningful in the longer run is for the National Taxi Association (NTA) to work with the taxi operators to innovate to meet the competition from private hire cars.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I trust that our workers will rise to the challenges and find a way to adapt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Some of our bus captains I have met in Punggol have upgraded themselves to take on interchange and operations control centre roles which allow them to continue improving the commuter experience in other ways and also upgrade their own incomes and responsibilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As I have shared earlier, taxi drivers have also been improving services in response to competition and I look forward to the evolving situation to improve overall point-to-point services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The second feature of our future transport system is that it will be greener.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Emissions from motor vehicles are one of the largest sources of air pollution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Vehicular emissions contribute about half of locally produced PM2.5 pollution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: A study postulates that nitrogen dioxide produced by diesel vehicles is linked to around 23,500 deaths in the UK a year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: London is setting up a Low Emissions Zone in its city centre to address this and is replacing most of its diesel buses with hybrid and electric ones.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The current CEVS grants rebates or levies surcharges based on a vehicle's carbon emissions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This will encourage buyers to choose models that are not only more fuel-efficient, but also emit less air pollutants, and thus further improve the ambient air quality and public health.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our colleagues from MEWR will elaborate on the enhancements to the scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will also make a shift towards a greener public bus fleet.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: By procuring buses which meet more stringent emission standards, we have already been greening most of our diesel-powered fleet.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But no emissions is better than low emissions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: That is why we have been trialling an electric bus on Service 17 and now Service 119.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked about the results of this trial.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The initial feedback has been encouraging; while more costly, commuters enjoyed the quieter ride and the bus has been fairly reliable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: However, a problem with pure-electric technology is that it is not fully proven yet for tropical climates, in part because vehicles operating here consume a lot of energy for air-conditioning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The electric car sharing and electric taxi trials that LTA launched recently will also help us better understand the application of this technology in our climate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The third feature of our future transport system is that it will be more inclusive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It must be designed thoughtfully to serve the needs of vulnerable groups, such as people with disabilities; families, especially those with young children; and an ageing population which is likely to be less mobile.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our journey towards a fully barrier-free public transport system is almost complete.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: All MRT stations and bus interchanges are now barrier-free.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Ninety-two percent of our public buses are wheelchair-accessible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This will increase to 98% by the end of next year, and 100% by 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I agree, however, with Ms Sylvia Lim that there is always room to improve.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We plan to do more, within what is affordable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also asked about derailment contingency.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Rail staff will assist to evacuate any person who needs help.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: SCDF will also be called on site to help further.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: If I recall correctly, late last year, there was one done for staff and SCDF to familiarise themselves in case of such derailment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: One idea that has also been suggested occasionally in this House is to have audio announcements on our buses to help passengers with visual disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: LTA will start testing this as an enhancement to the new passenger information display system currently being trialled on Service 106.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: LTA plans to collaborate with SG Enable for SG Enable to "adopt" Redhill MRT station, which is the station nearest to the Enabling Village and used by many of the disabled community to travel to the Village.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Redhill Station then can be a test-bed for new mobility technologies, ideas and infrastructure designs that can make public transport more accessible for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: So, this move can, hopefully, enable all to co-create solutions with people who are affected, including the Enabling Village community.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The journey from Redhill station to the Enabling Village is a challenge for persons with disabilities, because of the hilly topography and the 400-m distance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: So, I have challenged LTA and SG Enable to come up with a solution to improve this last mile and, hopefully, apply such solutioning to future projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Another frequent feedback is from families with young children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They want to have public transport made more accessible for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I know it is challenging to have to fold up strollers before boarding public buses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: On the other hand, LTA and the bus operators have genuine concerns for the safety of children in open strollers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: For example, if the bus, for whatever reason, has to brake suddenly or swerve suddenly, we are concerned for the child's safety.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But, on balance, we think we can move on this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We hope this will make travelling with young children on public transport more convenient.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Parents will have to be fully attentive and please take responsibility for the safety of the children and hold on tight to the open strollers at all times.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As we work towards a more inclusive public transport system, I urge other commuters to be patient if it takes a bit longer for families with open strollers to board our buses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Two, if the lifts were to be shut down for maintenance or repair, the crossings will no longer be barrier-free.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I think a better solution is to implement at-grade pedestrian crossings where safety is not an issue and the impact on traffic not excessive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: These are more convenient for the elderly and faster to build.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: With our Green Man Plus programme, the elderly and persons with disabilities can get more crossing time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Another way in which we are making streets safer for the elderly and the less mobile is through the Silver Zone programme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Currently, we have nine Silver Zones and feedback has been positive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked about the design and public education of Silver Zone features, including courtesy crossings.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Before building Silver Zones, LTA works closely with grassroots leaders to ensure that the design and safety features meet the needs of the residents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As part of the public education process, LTA distributes posters and brochures, and also makes use of community events to address residents' concerns face-to-face.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Indeed, pedestrian safety must always be a primary concern for MOT and, in this regard, I agree with Mr Dennis Tan and also with what Mr Png Eng Huat has raised on the importance of safe path-sharing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We are working to improve the safety aspect of our infrastructure design.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The location mentioned by Mr Tan is part of our plans to do so within the next two years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Besides infrastructural improvements, we have introduced new rules to protect pedestrians sharing footpaths with bicycles and PMDs, such as a speed limit of 15 kilometres per hour, as well as the maximum width and weight and top speed of devices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We have also introduced a new code of conduct to guide cyclists on how to share paths safely.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: But more than infrastructure upgrades and rules and regulations, we need the cooperation of all users in order to have shared spaces, to make them safe.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We need to develop a culture of gracious sharing through education efforts, amongst others.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Such education efforts are being expanded to more groups of users and in more languages, in line with what Mr Lim Biow Chuan has suggested.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: At the last Car-free Sunday, we announced that the new Safe Riding Programme will be expanded to riders of PMDs and power-assisted bicycles.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: And the programme curriculum can be found on the LTA website, with translations in Mandarin, Malay and Tamil to be available soon.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: To ensure compliance with the new rules and code of conduct, LTA has stepped up enforcement against reckless cyclists and PMD users.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: While the enforcement team is not very large, as Mr Lim has pointed out, they work very hard and intelligently.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Enforcement officers are deployed to hotspots, which are identified using data and, importantly, from public feedback.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In addition, the number of volunteers has increased to 700 and they are supporting our enforcement officers well.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In addition, officers from the Traffic Police and NParks have also stepped in to help in enforcement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Going forward, we will be augmenting our enforcement efforts with technology, such as CCTVs and body cameras.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We are investing heavily in upgrading our transport system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We depend on those who serve in the transport industry to make our everyday commute better, and I want to thank them for their hard work and dedication.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our future transport system will be one that is smarter, greener and more inclusive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We aim to give every Singaporean a variety of mobility options to meet different needs at different times, and at different stages of their lives.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We can count on having more convenient and reliable journeys.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We will enjoy cleaner air and safer shared services and spaces.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: I look forward to these improvements which will bring about an intelligent and sustainable transport system for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore acts as a regional air and sea transport hub.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Our forefathers had the foresight to build on our advantageous geographic location and sea trade was our first engine of growth.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Spices, rubber and other commodities produced regionally were shipped through Singapore's harbour and sent to other parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We have, indeed, come a long way since.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The concern on the ground is that our status as an air hub and regional port of call may be increasingly threatened by our regional peers.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Recently, the Chinese launched a rail freight service between China and London, thus providing a land route alternative to the traditional sea freight route between Europe and Asia.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As a small country, we must remain open and connected to the world, be it by air or sea.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is in line with the recommendations spelt out by the Committee on the Future Economy.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In fact, it was the first out of seven strategies to take the Singapore economy forward.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Committee recommends that we need to deepen and diversify our international connections and press on with open trade.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Against this backdrop, I would like to ask MOT to share its plans on how Singapore can maintain its position as the regional hub for air and sea trade flows.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: In addition, a new Malacca harbour, the Melaka Gateway, is being developed.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: What will be the impact of these ports on our sea hub status?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Would the Ministry also share an update on how we can strengthen Singapore's competitiveness as an air and sea hub?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: How will the Industry Transformation Maps for Air Transport and Sea Transport help Singapore to stay ahead, and when will these ITMs be launched?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: China, India and Indonesia are three of the five fastest-growing markets in terms of additional passengers.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: How are we tapping into the growth of these markets?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: That is 37% of global investment and the highest of any region in the world.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: From Beijing, Tokyo, Seoul, Hong Kong, Taipei to cities in India and the Middle East, airports are fast expanding to capture a slice of the rising long-haul business travels and intra-regional traffic boosted by low cost carriers.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Obviously, there are many economic spin-offs arising from a city's comprehensive and international connectivity.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Just as we have experienced in Singapore, a thriving air hub benefits directly not just the overhaul and maintenance industry, but also brings measurable benefits to other sectors, such as logistics, convention and exhibition, hospitality, financial, healthcare and so on.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: A vibrant air hub also renders Singapore ideal for regional headquarters operations.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Competition to be the premier air hub is, however, most intense.

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: How does MOT work with the industry players to map out a collective vision for our future?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Would MOT take on an industry-development role to evolve a comprehensive Industry Transformation Map?

speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
text: Could the Minister highlight the kind of new jobs Singaporeans can expect from being a vibrant air hub of the future?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Changi Airport Terminal 4, slated to open in the latter part of this year, will be our latest aviation investment to be realised.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: As part of the Committee on the Future Economy's (CFE) recommendations, aviation falls under one of the sectors identified to have an Industry Transformation Map to up productivity and workers' skills and to promote innovation and adoption of technology.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: How is the newest airport terminal a showcase of industry transformation?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: What are the efforts to develop and implement productivity initiatives for higher efficiencies in airport operations, such as baggage handling and cargo management, at Terminal 4?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: How are the roles of workers in Terminal 4 different from Terminals 1, 2 and 3?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: For example, will there be less reliance on manpower and manual work; and a bigger push for automation, self-serve counters for commuters and even the use of robotics?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The development is likely to challenge Singapore's position as the major trans-shipment hub and the new cruise ship jetty will also have an impact on cruise tourism in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: A November 2016 CNBC article stated outright that Malacca is eyeing a slice of Singapore's shipping business, and the new port's selling points are lower costs, less congestion and less stringent port rules.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: An academic paper, published in March 2016 by two researchers for the Institute of Developing Economies, sought to project and forecast the economic impact of the Kra Canal.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: In most scenarios, Singapore stood to suffer a negative impact.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Could the Minister provide a realistic analysis of these threats and their impact on Singapore's ports?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Would it divert trade from Singapore and to what extent?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: What is MOT's plan to strengthen the position of our ports?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are anchored by well-connected ports that link Singapore to the rest of the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As noted by Minister Khaw Boon Wan, they are both pillars and enablers of our economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our approach has been to plan ahead and yet remain responsive to new developments and market opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We invest heavily to develop infrastructure and human capital so that Singaporeans can take up the good jobs created.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Over the next 10-15 years, many of our infrastructure investments will take shape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, we will not need twice as many people.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Innovation and the intensive use of technology will transform the way people work and companies do business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui and Mr Lee Yi Shyan asked about the two sectors' Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: My response to Members' cuts will outline the three key strategies embedded in our ITMs that will strengthen the competitiveness of our aviation and maritime hubs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are: smarter ports, vibrant enterprise ecosystems and systematic manpower development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I should, of course, add that when we say manpower development, we include woman power also.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I note Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Zaqy Mohamad, Mr Yee Chia Hsing and Miss Cheng's concerns about the regional port developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given that it will take some time for the Malacca Gateway project to be fleshed out and the uncertainty surrounding the Kra Canal project, it is still too early to determine their impact on us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But international competition has never been far away from our aviation and maritime sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our starting point is that others can and will up their game.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Whatever the analysis, the only response that will serve our long-term interests is to keep improving to stay ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, it is not enough to build bigger ports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have two strong industry champions − PSA in maritime and Changi Airport Group (CAG) in aviation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, what kind of smarter ports are they developing?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Put simply, our smarter ports will apply advanced technologies to achieve scale that is matched by superior connectivity, efficiency and reliability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: You need scale but what you really want is to deliver superior connectivity, efficiency and reliability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In our seaport, it will not simply be about buying automated guided vehicles or installing automated cranes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Rather, it will be about advanced planning and optimisation of equipment deployment to allow the seamless transfer of containers from vessel to wharf, then to truck, then to yard and then vice versa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It may sound easy but is actually very difficult to execute.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a transhipment hub that is connected to over 600 other ports − if you take Shanghai, they are connected to under 300 ports; we are connected to over 600 ports − container movements here are much more complex than ports that mostly handle origin-destination cargo.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, cargo that is either coming out from your own port city or going into your port city.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Here we do transhipment, where we do connections for shippers, and the vessel calls involve mind-boggling permutations of synchronised unloading and reloading.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The complexity of container movements will increase as we enhance the connectivity of our port and attract higher volumes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: That is why PSA is studying the use of data analytics that will generate insights about the flow of vessels and containers, and test-bedding automation solutions that will optimise processes and the use of equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: What we learn at Pasir Panjang will be used in the planning of Tuas Terminal which, when fully developed, will have a capacity bigger than Tanjong Pagar, Keppel, Brani and Pasir Panjang Terminals combined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Likewise, the bigger challenge for us at Changi is Terminal 5 which, Members may recall, will have an eventual capacity bigger than Terminals 1, 2 and 3 combined.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will enable us to host more flight connections and tap the growth of civil aviation in the Asia Pacific region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked for an update on developments at Changi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: T4 will begin operations in the second half of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is a lot of testing going on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Planning for T5 is on track, and CAG will soon begin to identify the architects to take on the challenge of designing it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: T4, which is smaller than the existing terminals, is, in some ways, a testbed for T5.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On opening day, passengers will have a full suite of self-service and automated options for check-in, bag drop, immigration clearance and boarding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Airports elsewhere may have implemented some of these components, but not the entire suite as far as we know.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Beyond what passengers see, at the back-end, T4 will have automated baggage screening, sorting and storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Smart cleaning initiatives, centralised support functions for retail and F&B will further reduce the manpower needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The experiments at T4 will also shape what is possible at T5 in future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And I think that is where the bigger savings have to be.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our existing terminals, too, are raising their performance and productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: CAG and CAAS are bringing airport stakeholders onto a common collaborative decision-making platform to share operational data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For instance, airlines and ground handling agents now can view real-time flight movements on the airfield.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This helps them efficiently deploy resources to quickly rectify problems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This may seem negligible − just 90 seconds − but we must remember that we have about 1,000 aircraft movements in our airport every day.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, the cumulative impact on runway productivity and, of course, for the airlines, fuel cost savings are really not trivial, not at all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Why does it matter that PSA and CAG develop smarter ports?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ultimately, their customers, the shipping lines and airlines − and the end users − the shippers and passengers − they all vote with their feet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To keep the customers and end-users coming back, scale must be matched by superior connectivity, efficiency and reliability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is what will help Singapore to build a sustainable edge, which is exactly Mr Lee Yi Shyan's question.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For Singapore to extract the full value of our smarter ports, we will also need vibrant enterprise ecosystems and systematic manpower development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With well-connected ports as anchors, our maritime and aviation hubs have grown far beyond PSA and CAG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In aviation, Singapore is home to world-class air freight, aerospace, and maintenance, repair and overhaul companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When we ask companies why they choose to be in Singapore in spite of our higher costs, they tell us that it is the value of being plugged in into a vibrant network, a thriving ecosystem, if you will.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through this network, they can be closer to their customers and gain quick access to market intelligence which helps them make timely decisions to respond to market shifts: pricing, what to do with the commercial arrangements − all of these require intelligence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They can also find good partners more easily to share risks in business ventures or jointly develop new projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A vibrant enterprise ecosystem is a natural magnet that attracts and retains more businesses to weave a denser network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we actively seek to anchor key players across many types of aviation and maritime services in Singapore − to stay relevant and strengthen our hub competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our international maritime centre continues to grow in breadth and depth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through new joint ventures with PSA, major shipping lines, like CMA-CGM and China COSCO Shipping, are shifting more of their activities to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is helpful that both CMA-CGM and China COSCO are also leaders in the ever-shifting landscape of alliance partnerships among the container lines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When the companies open up new lines of businesses, it enables our aviation and maritime hubs to capture emerging opportunities and stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take, for example, the movement of time- and temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With this, companies like Global Airfreight International, SATS and SIA Cargo will be better placed to benefit from the growth in pharmaceutical trade as the region becomes more affluent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But perhaps the biggest value of vibrant enterprise ecosystems is that they help Singapore's drive for innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This year, we will see the results of our first two Aviation Challenges, one of which focuses on automating baggage handling for narrow-body aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Members know, the process today is largely automated − screening, sorting, storage − but still has some parts that require manual handling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Behind the scenes, bags have to be transferred from a baggage carousel to a baggage trolley which is towed to the aircraft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They are then unloaded and moved into the aircraft belly hold, which, for a narrow-body aircraft, is 11 metres deep but just one metre high.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We ought to salute our baggage handlers who do this back-breaking work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we should not leave this process unchanged.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We searched all over the world for solutions, but found none that would fully meet our needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, we resolved to develop our own solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As we speak, five teams from industry and academia are developing prototypes to automate this laborious process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Platforms like Aviation Challenges are attempts by CAAS to bring together the best minds to develop innovative solutions for our airport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But these attempts will not succeed unless we have a vibrant enterprise ecosystem to draw on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The first two challenges have drawn on the capabilities of over 100 engineers and researchers from several entities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are involving local companies, such as Cyclect Electrical Engineering and ST Dynamics, and I have asked CAAS and CAG to bring more on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is not just the airport that will gain from the innovations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses, too, can capture value through deepening their capabilities and spinning off other innovative products and services to support their internationalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Take, for example, Ascenz Solutions which started in 2008 as a two-person show.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With co-funding from MPA's Maritime Innovation and Technology Fund, Ascenz created a system called Shipulse that collates data from sensors installed on board ships and transmits it back to shore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Shipulse allows shipowners to remotely analyse a ship's speed and fuel efficiency in real-time and then instruct the crew to adjust the ship's route or carry out energy efficiency measures to save fuel and improve vessel performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Having expanded to a team of more than 30 with operations in nine countries, Ascenz is now eyeing the European market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A likely shift towards digitalisation in the aviation and maritime sectors can give more start-ups like Ascenz their big breaks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: You know, this is serious stuff, when even an established giant like AP Moller-Maersk decides to nominate as its new Chairman someone with a track record as "Mr Digitalisation".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is going to be a harbinger of major industry transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Interestingly, the maritime sector is not usually thought of as a beacon of innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But I am bullish about the prospects for Singapore because the market here for innovative products and services is significant and quickly evolving.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As their innovations gain market acceptance in Singapore, start-ups will be in a stronger position to internationalise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PSA has already taken the lead by launching PSA unboXed last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And what PSA unboXed does is to invite start-ups and potential partners to propose technology solutions for the port, in which PSA unboXed may then decide to take an equity stake and try to make a success of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have asked MPA to work with SPRING to see how best to expose more local start-ups to opportunities in maritime businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The MPA Living Lab will provide the essential "live" operating conditions that will facilitate the test-bedding of potential innovations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Because this is critical − you can have a great idea, but if you are not able to prove the concept in "live" operating conditions, that would be a gap in the innovation journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Areas being explored include autonomous vessels, multi-purpose drones and next-generation vessel traffic management systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We believe this could be a game-changer for Singapore, bringing together technology developers and industry players to anchor their innovation activities in Singapore and help our sea hub stay ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Smarter ports and more vibrant enterprise ecosystems bring many more good jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The jobs created over the next decade will be markedly different from today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The increasing deployment of smart technologies means that new jobs will be more knowledge-intensive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the port, more data scientists and operations research analysts will be needed to optimise shipping routes, port operations and vessel traffic management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the airport, we will require data scientists skilled in air traffic operations research and analysis, to optimise our runway and airspace capacities through modelling and simulation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Technology will also transform existing jobs into higher skill, higher value-added jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For instance, port equipment engineers today are responsible for maintaining and repairing the port's equipment and facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With the introduction of AGVs, they will also plan and design operations to segregate manned and unmanned activities and to synchronise the AGVs' operations with other automated equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also investing in baggage and cargo robotics systems at the airport that will leave the more repetitive tasks of lifting and loading to the machines, freeing up our workers to oversee other parts of the operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are committed to helping Singaporeans make the most of the exciting and rewarding career opportunities, by working closely with our tripartite partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For fresh school-leavers, CAAS and MPA are working with the Institutes of Higher Learning to develop new industry-specific training schemes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The next intake for these two programmes is scheduled for April this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Three other Earn and Learn Programmes were launched last year for port operations officers, deck officers and marine engineers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are also helping mid-career Singaporeans switch to maritime and aviation careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To prepare them for roles in flight operations, baggage, catering, maintenance and cargo, Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) will provide structured training and career progression, with corresponding salary increases.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: PCPs for more occupations will be launched in due course.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For Singaporeans already in the aviation and maritime sectors, we will help them progress in their careers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MPA will enhance the Maritime Cluster Fund for Manpower Development to support a wider range of training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To help Singaporeans better plan their careers, we will develop Skills Frameworks that help them identify those which are relevant and necessary for advancement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A Skills Framework will also be developed for the Air Transport sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But let me make clear that we cannot make this work without the companies taking an active interest and the workers being willing to adapt.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, tripartite involvement and commitment will be key.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will, therefore, continue to promote a region that stays open and connected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Open sea lines of communications, too, are critical to trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, almost half of the world's seaborne trade by tonnage passes through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, and we must ensure that these waters remain safe and secure for ships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through MPA's Safety@Sea campaign, the number of marine incidents has been kept low.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There was only one major shipping incident in our waters in 2016, no easy feat, considering that Singapore is one of the world's busiest ports with over 130,000 vessel calls every year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also look to more environmentally-friendly and sustainable growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, CAAS has worked with neighbouring airports to develop an Air Traffic Flow Management System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It sounds a bit abstract − Air Traffic Flow Management System.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But what it really means is that you want to regulate the flow of aircraft even before they take off from the departure airports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Because we want to have more certainty in managing, at the receiving airports, the incoming flights.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To passengers, what this would mean is that you could spend less time circling in the air before landing because the airport is congested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But to airlines, the fuel cost savings is very much appreciated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With more than 150,000 landings at Changi each year, the cumulative effect on the environment is quite significant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the maritime side, MPA already has the Maritime Singapore Green Initiative with five programmes − the Green Ship, Green Port, Green Technology, Green Awareness and Green Energy Programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: MPA has been working with industry and like-minded ports around the world to harmonise LNG bunkering processes and to grow a global network of LNG-ready ports.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is no use if we are LNG-ready but other ports are not.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These efforts have seen good progress, with authorities in Japan, Korea and Norway recently coming on board.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about our response to oil spills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are highly vigilant towards environmental incidents and have a well-established, multi-agency response plan which is regularly exercised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: During the oil spill off Pasir Gudang in January, agencies responded swiftly and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Within hours, MPA, which is the coordinator for the inter-agency response, had already modelled the spilled oil's trajectory and worked with the agencies to take measures, such as laying out oil-absorbent booms, to prevent its spread.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a result, traffic in the East Johor Straits and Singapore's port operations were not affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Affected beaches were quickly cleaned up and key biodiversity areas at Pulau Ubin, Coney Island and Pasir Ris were protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are now working with the insurers of the vessels responsible for the incident to compensate the affected parties, including the fish farms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bunker Convention puts the responsibility on the shipowners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will strive to strengthen the competitiveness of our air and sea hubs through Smarter Ports, more Vibrant Enterprise Ecosystems and Systematic Manpower Development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through initiatives, like the Aviation Challenges and MPA Living Lab, we will help the businesses in these sectors help themselves by deepening their capabilities and developing innovative products and services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Through tripartite cooperation and enhanced funding support, we will help Singaporeans acquire and master the deep skills that are needed to stay relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our officers have been working quietly but tirelessly, and I am mighty proud of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Whether in 10, 20 or 50 years, we still want to be leading aviation and maritime hubs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our businesses and workers will have every opportunity to be at the frontier of the industry transformations and ride this wave of growth.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarification.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: He mentioned earlier that he found that the calls made to taxi operators being rather ineffective and already overtaken by disruption.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Therefore, I would like to ask if he will work with LTA to remove Call Catering from the Quality of Standard yardstick measurement for taxi operators.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I did not say anything about calls being ineffective.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Earlier, the Minister mentioned that people calling up taxi operators for the person over the other side of the phone to book a taxi, that being relatively overtaken by third-party apps and the likes of other bookings.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: One to Minister Ng for replying to my cut on dynamic pricing.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am all for dynamic pricing and companies innovating with new models.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But my question was how LTA, as a regulator, will ensure that in shifting to demand pricing, you do not have a deja vu of taxi availability being an issue, because that could shift behaviour in terms of how taxis make themselves available.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The second question is I thank the Minister also for demystifying the slow bus-driving for some services like 983 where you travel from between Choa Chu Kang and Bukit Panjang.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Residents have complained that buses sometimes travel at 30km/h or 40km/h on an empty road or stop at bus stops where there is no one.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Are these service levels determined by LTA or the service provider?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Despite repeated feedback, does LTA review the service level based on commuters' experience?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I understand these projects compete for resources within the LTA budget but if you could give residents and citizens clarity on how they can qualify and when they qualify, I think they are more inclined to —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Zaqy, just the clarification, please, no speeches.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The Public Transport Council and the taxi companies are still in discussion.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will watch the situation carefully to monitor taxi availability whenever the programme is instituted.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, as we let it evolve, as always, we will monitor, review and see what is to be done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To answer the Member Mr Zaqy's query, and relying on memory, I think it is 67 decibels.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I am relying on memory; I am 65 years old.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, if you keep your clarifications short, the front bench will remember them better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Is the service level determined by LTA or the service provider?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Could they be adjusted based on commuters' experience?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It is always a collective effort that we want to ensure the best service to commuters.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: When we involve this technology, it is still dependent on real-time traffic conditions.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: You can imagine in peak hours, I have got three buses that start from the depot.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: From the very start, the first bus collects more passengers, it actually slows down along the whole route; whereas the second bus coming through, where there are less passengers, let us say a headway of five, 10 minutes, the second bus actually catches up.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: You can imagine if we have more than three buses and you have a peak-hour period of two hours of this bunching and relaxing.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, the real-time data is needed for them to adjust and this will be a real-time operator responsibility.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But LTA will see what we can do to facilitate this use of technology, as I have said.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier, he spoke about the steps to make the public transport system more inclusive for disabled passengers as well as families.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And he mentioned a new scheme where families would be allowed to bring children in strollers on board, rather than to have to fold up their strollers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to clarify whether, actually, he would agree that this ties in nicely with my cut on wheelchair space because you would need more space on the buses now for these various wheelchairs, prams and so on, and that the Government will bear this in mind when it looks at the design of buses.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The short answer is yes because they are similar.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In the current wheelchair-accessible buses that we have, more than 5,000 of them, there is at least one available space for wheelchair or stroller.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Minister Ng, you said that electric buses are costlier than regular buses.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: First, is this in terms of operational cost or capital cost?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Third, whether this will eventually factor into fare increases, especially with the revision of the fare adjustment mechanism which is due this year?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I do not have the numbers offhand but in terms of capital expenditure (capex) and operational expenditure (opex), yes, they are more expensive.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In a trial stage, right now, we have not raised any fares; they are still consistent with whatever the fares are for the rest of the buses.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, realistically, whether we go green or not, we will have to be realistic about fare prices in the long term.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I just want to follow up on the clarification by Mr Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I suppose he was referring to the Bus Service Reliability Framework which is really a good intention by LTA to keep the bus to the timings and to arrive punctually and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But what happens on the ground, sometimes, is that the bus may arrive too early and then, therefore, they stop at the bus stop for a while or they slow down the speed of the travelling and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is causing disservice to the commuters instead.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Where the bus may have to slow down, it may inconvenience some.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: But in terms of the overall system of buses plying the whole three-hour route, the overall service to more passengers is better.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Indeed, some commuters may notice that this bus is slowing down but it gives proper spacing between buses.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In a long route, it prevents bunching of buses that if you miss the two buses, you have to wait a long, long time for the third bus to come.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: Good to know that we are staying competitive by offering smarter technology solutions to our stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: However, I also know that some of our air and sea agencies have a consulting arm that offer their technology know-how to other countries.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: CAI does not, in particular, hold intellectual property rights with regards to, say, technology.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What they do have is great operational insights.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: When it was set up, the idea was that, as part of Singapore enterprises internationalising, there was also benefit in having CAI offer their expertise to airports elsewhere that would like to tap into this expertise.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But I take the Member's point; we want to keep some of the crown jewels.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The entities that are involved in this are equally mindful about it.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: He earlier mentioned that the implementation of the tiered ARF is to further suit the implementation of tiered ARF for cars in 2013, basically, to have some form of consistency.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: My clarification is, similarly, on the basis of consistency, would the Minister consider having PARF rebate for motorcycles?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As for PARF, PARF's main purpose is to incentivise deregistration.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I seek a clarification from Senior Minister of State Mrs Josephine Teo.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Can I just ask the Senior Minister of State what is the Government's view on the likely competition that may be posed by the recent opening of the China-Britain freight train, at least, in the future years?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It took them 18 days, which is about half of what it would take if the same set of containers were to have to travel by ship.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, there is obviously some value in that because there may be some types of cargo which will be too expensive to transport by air.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But, if you transport it by sea, then it takes twice as long.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, items could include things like prototypes that you want to deliver to the market very quickly.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But this type of transportation − rail transportation − is constrained by the scale.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This particular voyage that was undertaken, if I remember correctly, involved 40-foot containers − bigger boxes − but there were just 344 of them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If you compare that to what one of the mega-vessels would take these days, that is, closer to 18,000 to 19,000 TEUs, the scale that can be transported is completely different.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the landscape is always evolving and we will have to pay close attention.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One other area that really deserves close attention is the Arctic Circle.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: With the melting of the icecaps, I think Mr Dennis Tan would know that the northern sea route offers something compelling, too.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is just that, in the foreseeable future, it is not likely.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the foreseeable future, it is not likely that even though you are able to sail through, you can cut up to 60% of the voyage time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It would be very difficult to schedule services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We watch all of these developments very closely, including the Kra Canal, which has been talked about for decades actually.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The short answer to your question is that we monitor all of these.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do analyse what their impact could be.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But, as I have said in my earlier speech, we cannot stop others from upping their game.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We just have to do everything within our power to stay ahead.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: It is exciting to learn that the Tuas Terminal would be a state-of-the-art smart port.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I hope the Senior Minister of State can elaborate on the transport infrastructure linking to the Tuas Port.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Otherwise, the new port can be large but few workers would like to work there.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ang is not just a good Member of Parliament, he is also a very good adviser to the union.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, please be assured that this is very much on our minds.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I appreciate that the agencies are working together but can we have a roundtable so that the agencies can work together with the other stakeholders and experts − the NGOs and the scientific community − for oil spills?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Ng, roundtable or not, we will meet with them.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, do you wish to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Further, on behalf of Members, I extend our gratitude and appreciation to Mr Khaw Boon Wan, Second Minister Ng Chee Meng and Senior Minister of State Mrs Josephine Teo for answering our questions and sharing with us MOT's plans for the future.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: On that note, Madam, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
